title: Convergent toolflow ergonomics: deterministic injection, parallel reconciliation, and retry surface
author: Priya Narang
release_notes: Improves tool-calling ergonomics: deterministic result injection for multi-tool pipelines, parallel reconciliation with bounded fanout, and a developer-facing retry surface. No breaking API changes. Recommended rollout to canary before full production.
description:
Context and motivation: We have several customer patterns that combine multiple tool calls inside a single chat turn: parallel lookups (user profile + permissions), speculative enrichment (NER + web search), and chained transforms (summarize -> format). In some of these cases, the runtime previously returned non-deterministic injection ordering and duplicate re-injections after retries, which caused frontend flakiness and made downstream structured-output validation brittle. This PR introduces a cohesive ergonomics layer for multi-tool flows that focuses on three goals: 1) deterministic injection semantics (order and idempotency keys), 2) a reconciliation strategy for parallel tool results that constrains fanout and attaches provenance metadata, and 3) an explicit developer-facing retry surface that avoids duplicate payloads and maintains streaming stability.

What this changes (high-level): - Adds a deterministic injection protocol: tools are assigned stable invocation IDs, and the runtime tracks insertion points so that on resume/retry the same logical positions are used. This prevents content shuffling when partial streaming responses are resumed. - Parallel reconciliation operator: a new executor that accepts multiple tool futures, applies configurable merge policies (first-wins, priority-map, merge-by-field), and emits a single canonical injection block with provenance headers. - Retry surface: explicit retry annotations on tool descriptors (max_retries, backoff_policy, idempotency_hint) and centralized retry coordinator that deduplicates in-flight retries using the invocation ID and at-most-once commit semantics for side-effecting tools. - Compatibility shim: small OpenAI-compat layer change to preserve function_call ordering when tools are returned as an array; structured output helpers expanded to attach tool provenance (tool_id, invocation_id, latency_ms) so downstream evals can assert stability.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-1892 linked - [x] Unit tests for injection semantics - [x] Integration test for parallel reconciliation (includes edge cases for duplicate tool results) - [x] E2E streaming test to ensure resume doesn't reorder injections - [x] Backcompat tests for OpenAI compatibility layer - [x] Docs: console docs + SDK surface notes

Commits (summary): - 9f1c2b0: introduce invocation-id allocation and tracking - 4b3a7de: parallel-reconciler executor and merge policies - a6d4f11: retry coordinator and idempotency dedupe table - 2c7e9b4: openai-compat: preserve function_call array order + add provenance fields - e5d2a90: tests + fixtures for multi-tool flows - 1b7d033: docs and examples for TypeScript/CLI quickstarts

Files/areas touched (high-level): - runtime/executor/reconciler.py (new) - runtime/invocation/id_allocator.py (new) - runtime/retry/coordinator.go (new) - api/openai_compat/handler.ts - sdk/typescript/src/tools.ts (small surface additions) - tests/integration/multi_tool_reconcile.test.ts - docs/console/toolflows.md

Review conversation (highlights): - Jason Lee (reviewer): "Overall design looks solid. Concern about memory growth in the dedupe table for long-lived flows; suggest LRU or TTL eviction. Also please add a metric for 'injection_reorders' so we can detect regressions in canary." - Priya (author): "Added TTL-based eviction (configurable per deployment) and an internal metric injection.reorder.count. See retry/coordinator.go lines ~120-160. Will surface to Console dashboard in a follow-up if we want a default chart." - Marina Kovács: "Merge policy set is flexible — can we expose 'merge-by-key' in the SDK with a small helper? Frontends need to prefer first-wins for some use cases." - Priya: "Added merge helper in sdk/typescript/tools.ts export mergeByKey and updated quickstart example." - Owen Park: "One nit: OpenAI compat preserves order but we introduced an additional provenance wrapper; make sure it doesn't break existing parser libs that expect raw function_call objects." - Priya: "Compat shim emits an optional _provenance field; existing SDKs ignore unknown keys. Added an extra opt-in flag in openai_compat handler to disable provenance for strict parity." - CI flakiness: initial CI run failed two flaky streaming tests; rerun fixed it and logs included an added 50ms sleep in the test harness to stabilize race windows.

CI summary: - unit: pass - integration: pass (with retry flakiness fixed) - lint: pass - e2e streaming: pass - security scan: pass

Performance notes: Local benchmarks on a small canary (r4 nodes) show median tail latency increase of ~1.8% for single-tool calls (due to id allocation overhead) and a 12-18% improvement in aggregate latency for common parallel-lookup patterns because reconciliation reduces duplicate downstream processing. Cost tradeoffs documented in ENG-2034.

Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated for a small set of customers with multi-tool usage for 2 weeks - Monitor injection.reorder.count, tool.invocation.latency, and retry.dedupe.rate - Gradual rollout to hosted API with a feature flag controlling provenance and reconciliation behavior - SDK release (TS) coordinated: minor bump with helper and example changes

Merge: squashed and merged by Priya Narang via squash-merge. Merge commit: "squash: convergent toolflow ergonomics — deterministic injection + reconciliation + retry surface".

Notes and follow-ups: - Add a dashboard tile in Console for injection stability (ENG-2140) - Optional opt-out API for provenance for strict OpenAI parity - Explore bounded memory advisory to surface to customers with very long-lived sessions
notes: Author ensured backcompat path: provenance opt-out and no change to existing function_call payload shape unless opt-in. Key metric injection.reorder.count introduced for monitoring.
